# Module, IPC and worker boundary review data

These hand-authored synthetic cases support [N0-09 issue 15](https://github.com/whoodes/namtab/issues/15) and the canonical [runtime boundary contract](../../../docs/engine/runtime-persistence-security.md#n0-09-boundary-review-and-test-ownership). The runtime page owns semantics and test responsibilities; this directory owns review examples, provenance and integrity. No terminal package, decoder, worker transport, launch policy or test implementation is delivered. No case is a passing runtime result, accepted admission tuple or NG0 decision.

- `imports.json` challenges future pure-library/worker/client dependencies, private exports, unsafe seams and the preserved seven-Rust/four-TS foundation. Six Rust crates are covered by active-source Clippy/tests; the historical engine remains a workspace member.
- `ipc.json` gives raw framing/duplicate-key/identity/FD/error cases and exact-bound/one-beyond recipes for the proposed private decoder review tuple. Raw JSON fragments are strings intentionally preserving ambiguous keys for a future raw-byte decoder; parsing the outer fixture does not test them. Their member spellings illustrate the private binding and do not define wire DTOs. Public N0-06 fields/limits remain owned by its contract.
- `faults.json` challenges two sessions sharing a worker, independent pipe facts, emergency controls, bounded fairness/backpressure, capture gaps and the difference between live-owner attach and crash restore.

All strings, identifiers, apparent secrets and failures are invented for review on 2026-10-16. Nothing is captured from a user, host environment or process, and no upstream code/corpus/data is included. Payloads contain no real credentials, paths, transcripts or executable artifacts. Embedded snippets are inert data, never commands to run. The cases derive from the repository's native receipt/writer, finite core, security, recovery and runtime owners, not from measured product behavior. No dependencies, package manifests/locks, licenses, historical oracle or evidence bytes are changed.

`manifest.json` records SHA-256 integrity, origin and R/V traceability for these three payloads. Manifest/JSON/link checks prove review-data consistency only; they do not implement preallocation bounds, authentication, FD containment, fairness or recovery. A future executable harness must independently challenge each expectation, establish its positive setup before negative probes, and record the evaluated source/build/runtime/resource tuple. Real process/transport/fault tests and owner resource admission remain open. Do not regenerate expectations to fit an implementation. N0-06 integration, two fresh reviews and NG0 owner acceptance are still required.
